links.outcome: LLM response evidence-based quality across prompts varying in informedness (keywords vs generic vs omitted)
links.effect: More informed prompting gave higher scores: MAPPinfo F(2,351)=40.25, p<0.001, ηp2=0.19; ebmNucleus F(2,351)=528.41, p<0.001, ηp2=0.75. Response quality was contingent on prompt phrasing.
links.quote: Our systematic variation of prompt informedness revealed the expected pattern across the tested LLMs (Fig. 1a–c ), demonstrating that more informed prompting led to higher scores according to both assessment schemes MAPPinfo ( F (2,351) = 40.25, p < 0.001, η p 2 = 0 . 19 ) and ebmNucleus ( F (2,351) = 528.41, p < 0.001, η p 2 = 0 . 75 ).

links.outcome: Compliance of LLM screening information with best-available evidence and evidence-based communication criteria
links.effect: Even with expert-informed prompts, under 50% of maximum compliance for ChatGPT and Gemini; laypeople's control prompts reached ~17% (MAPPinfo) and 13% (ebmNucleus) of maximum score.
links.quote: Even when well-informed prompts were crafted by researchers—ensuring maximum accordance with information requirements—not even 50% of maximum compliance could be reached with ChatGPT and Gemini responses (somewhat better in Le Chat).

links.outcome: Quality of LLM information elicited by laypeople with a minimal prompting boost (OARS) vs control
links.effect: Boost moderately improved quality (MAPPinfo F(1,294)=15.26, ηp2=0.05; ebmNucleus F(1,294)=12.12, ηp2=0.04) but remained below required standards; control reached ~17% and 13% of maximum.
links.quote: The boosting intervention for more informed prompting moderately improved the quality of elicited health information across all LLMs (Fig. 2a–c ), as indicated by ANOVA main effects for MAPPinfo ( F (1,294) = 15.26, p < 0.001, η p 2 = 0 . 05 ) and ebmNucleus ( F (1,294) = 12.12, p = 0.001, η p 2 = 0 . 04 ).

links.outcome: Information quality by user education and LLM experience in laypeople's prompting
links.effect: Higher education (β=0.16, p=0.032) and more LLM experience (β=0.26, p=0.007) gave higher quality; frequent health-information LLM use was negatively associated (β=-0.25, p=0.009).
links.quote: However, more frequent LLM usage for seeking health information was negatively associated with information quality ( β = −0.25, p = 0.009).
